title: Model catalog stability decision tree and rollback sentinels for open model intake
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Community/open model intake has become the largest source of variance in our hosted model catalogue—variants show different micro-benchmarks, tokenization edgecases, and sometimes incompatible operator kernels. Current intake guidance is fragmented (PRDs, ad-hoc notes, and engineer mental models). Goal: produce a prescriptive, executable requirements set that (1) defines a stability/compatibility decision tree for new open model variants, (2) defines version pinning semantics and fallback rules that are machine-checkable, and (3) defines rollback sentinels and monitoring hooks required before and after making an unpinned variant available. Scope: product requirements and acceptance criteria for the intake flow, CI gating rules, console metadata fields (compat_level, pin_reason, pin_window), and operator runbook items. Out of scope: implementation details inside runtime kernels and per-hardware quantization docs (these will be referenced).
acceptance_criteria: A canonical stability decision tree document exists (single-page flowchart + textual rules) and is approved by Eng and Runtime leads
Pinning semantics are specified such that the catalog UI and deployment automation can: accept 'pinned' = {major,major.minor} and 'unpin-window' metadata; policy is machine-parseable
CI gating checks are defined and their failure modes documented: perf-regression threshold, op-compatibility mismatch, tokenizer-diff > 0.5%

Console exposes three new metadata fields for catalog entries: compat_level (stable|candidate|experimental), pin_reason (string), pin_window_end (ISO date or empty), and these fields are surfaced in the API contract
Rollback sentinels: list of 4 monitoring hooks (latency SLO breach, token-error spike, output-entropy shift, crash-rate) are defined with thresholds and linked Alert runbook IDs
Two community-sourced models (one LLM small/fast, one LLM large) are onboarded using the new checklist, with a post-onboard runbook sign-off from engineering
Product and SE playbooks updated with step-by-step onboarding checklist and sample message templates for customers affected by pin changes
notes: Trade-off: stricter pinning reduces accidental regressions but increases fragmentation and storage overhead; proposal favors pin-major by default with opt-in pin-minor where backwards-compatibility risk is high
Decision: prefer machine-readable pin metadata to free-text pin reasons; free-text allowed but must be accompanied by a short enumerated tag
Edgecase: models that change tokenizer behavior require a flagged migration path and cannot be auto-unpinned for 30 days post-release
We will reuse existing runtime telemetry (trace IDs + perf histograms) and add two new metrics: compat_token_diff_ratio and pinned_variant_uptime
